title: Persistent Methane Plumes as Equipment Sales Leads
one_liner: Sell satellite-detected methane emitters to the vendors who profit from fixing them: a lead-gen engine, not a compliance tool.
customer: Vapor-recovery-unit makers, flare-gas-to-power microturbine and genset vendors, landfill gas-collection contractors, dairy digester and RNG developers, and small gas gatherers or offtakers. Roughly 2,000 companies in the US; first buyers are sales VPs at 20-person equipment firms.
problem: Abatement vendors prospect blind at trade shows. Emitters are often unaware of a persistent leak or vent, or they do not know its dollar value. A 500 kg/h plume is roughly 230,000 MMBtu a year, or about $0.7M of saleable gas at $3/MMBtu. Methane data today is sold to regulators, ESG buyers and the emitters themselves, and none of them are motivated.
solution: A weekly ranked lead list of persistent emitters, defined as repeated detections across passes from open Carbon Mapper, EMIT and Tanager plume products, with GHGSat tasking to confirm the best leads. Each lead joins the plume to facility ownership (state permits, landfill and EPA datasets), wasted-gas value per year, distance to pipeline or grid, and likely fix type. Delivered as a CRM feed plus a one-page dossier.
why_now: Plume data is now abundant and partly free: Carbon Mapper's Tanager publishes public plume products, and GHGSat is expanding to 16+ satellites. With US federal methane-penalty pressure pushed out, pitches built on fines are weak, while pitches built on recovering saleable gas still work. Cheap gas-to-power gensets and microturbines are also more available.
revenue_model: $2k to $6k a month per vendor per basin or vertical. Success fee of 2% to 4% of first-year equipment or service revenue on closed leads, capped. Later, sell offtake and RNG-interconnect leads to gas buyers.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats a methane plume as a violation to be reported. It is really an unmonetized commodity with a known street address and a quantifiable price. Selling the plume to the person who profits from fixing it inverts the market and does not depend on regulation.
first_30_days: Pull open plume data for the Permian, Appalachia and Ohio/Pennsylvania landfills and build the top 100 persistent emitters. Hand-verify ownership and gas value on each. Cold-offer 25 equipment vendors and landfill gas contractors three free leads, then $3k a month. Ask for a paid pilot from 3 by day 30.

title: Serial-Level Collateral Registry for GPU Lenders
one_liner: The independent field-exam firm and cross-lender double-pledge registry for AI hardware debt, built on the military rule that a serial number appears on one hand receipt only.
customer: Private-credit funds, banks, equipment lessors, ABS trustees and insurers financing neocloud GPU fleets, which now hold well over $20 billion in GPU-backed debt. Secondary: neoclouds that need audit-ready proof to borrow at lower spreads.
problem: Lenders rely on borrower-supplied serial lists, telemetry and occasional inspections. After the Tricolor and First Brands double-pledging scandals (the SEC charged Tricolor's former executives in August 2026), lenders know 'the same collateral pledged twice' is real. GPU servers sit in multi-tenant colocation halls, are easy to move, swap or re-pledge to another SPV, and telemetry can be spoofed. Serial-number UCC filings are rarely searched across lenders, and a colo technician paid by the borrower is not an independent counter.
solution: Three layers. (1) A repeatable two-person independent inventory protocol: witnessed reads of chassis label, BMC out-of-band serial and GPU-level serial, plus rack and cage photos, location and power draw. (2) Serialized tamper-evident seals on cages and rack doors, checked at each visit. (3) A privacy-preserving cross-lender registry of hashed serials so a lender learns whether a serial is already pledged elsewhere without revealing its book. Deliver monthly compliance packages that plug into the loan's reporting covenants for the trustee.
why_now: GPU-backed lending crossed $20 billion, and CoreWeave's $8.5 billion delayed-draw term loan (March 2026) showed the asset class reaching investment-grade structures. Tricolor and First Brands made 'verify the collateral independently' a board-level demand in private credit. Loan documents already grant lenders inspection rights, so the buyer has the access but not the in-house field-exam capability. Export-control diversion risk adds a second reason for chain-of-custody evidence.
revenue_model: Per-site audit of $15-50k, annual monitoring retainer of $50-250k per facility, registry subscriptions of $50-200k per lender, and trustee or insurer reporting packages. Long-term, per-basis-point fees on financed collateral under verification.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud lives at the seam between paper and physical, and the only reliable control is a count by someone who does not report to the borrower. That is what a military property book officer and a sensitive-item inventory do. Lenders will not share collateral lists with each other but will share hashes to avoid being second in line, so the registry becomes the moat. Telemetry proves a box is powered on, not that it is the box you financed.
first_30_days: Recruit 2-3 former property book or supply officers plus a data-center operations technician. Write and publish the audit protocol. Approach 5 mid-tier credit funds and equipment lenders (not the giants) that do GPU deals and lack field-exam staff. Offer a fixed-fee pilot audit on a live deal using the lender's existing inspection rights. Get a securities and privacy lawyer to bless the hashed-serial registry design before any lender data is pooled.

title: Status-Cliff Benefit Sold Through PEOs
one_liner: A confidential, employer-paid benefit that screens temporary-status workers for alternate immigration relief, tracks work-authorization cliffs, and pre-arranges counsel and family plans before a raid, TPS termination or EAD lapse hits.
customer: Payroll, PEO and staffing firms serving labor-intensive employers (home health, poultry and meat processing, hospitality, warehousing, construction, agriculture), plus the employers themselves. They pay $4-9 per employee per month or $60-120 per screened worker.
problem: Employers with workers on TPS, humanitarian parole, pending asylum EADs or DACA are losing headcount unpredictably. Terminations of TPS and parole programs hit hundreds of thousands of workers with little warning, and automatic EAD extensions ended for renewals filed after late October 2025, so employees now fall out of I-9 validity while renewals are pending. Worksite enforcement and I-9 Notices of Inspection (3 business days to respond) are rising. HR treats it as a compliance chore, then loses 10-30% of a shift overnight.
solution: A benefit package in four parts. (1) A dashboard that projects the work-authorization cliff by employee category and date, with I-9 reverification scripts that avoid discriminatory over-documentation. (2) Confidential relief screening done by a licensed partner attorney for each willing employee (family petitions, pending asylum, U/T visas, SIJS, cancellation, adjustment eligibility) with the employee, not the employer, as the client. (3) An emergency file for each participating worker: signed G-28 on file, memorized A-number card, standby guardianship documents for children, and a hotline for the first 72 hours after a detention. (4) An I-9 pre-audit and a 72-hour Notice of Inspection response playbook.
why_now: TPS and parole terminations, the end of EAD automatic extensions, expanded enforcement, and increased I-9 audits all converged in late 2025 through 2026. Employers can no longer treat immigration compliance as an annual checkbox, and existing I-9 software only tracks expiry dates. It offers no relief screening, no emergency response, and no employee-side counsel.
revenue_model: Per-employee-per-month benefit fee split between the platform and partner law firms (structured as payment to the firm for services rendered, with the third-party-payor consent required by the professional conduct rules), plus per-screening fees and a premium I-9 audit-defense add-on. PEOs and payroll firms get a distribution margin.
non_obvious_insight: The employer's real loss is churn, not fines. In screenings, a surprisingly large share of workers, often a quarter or more in my experience, have a path they never knew about, because no one ever asked in a confidential setting. A worker who is told they have a path stays loyal to the employer that offered it. The right buyer is the PEO's benefits desk, since PEOs already sell legal-plan and EAP riders through one procurement decision.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical (home health agencies, where TPS and parole terminations are hitting staffing hardest) and one state. Partner with 2 immigration firms that have screening capacity. Pitch 3 regional agencies and 1 PEO with a 60-day pilot: 100 employees screened for $6,000, delivered as a de-identified summary of how many have alternate paths. Use the pilot data (headcount saved, cases opened) as the sales deck for the PEO channel.

title: Subsurface Desert Mapping From Free Radar Satellites
one_liner: Use open L-band radar data to map buried channels and structures beneath arid ground for mineral and water explorers.
customer: Junior critical-mineral explorers, uranium and lithium prospectors, groundwater drillers, national geological surveys and arid-region water utilities.
problem: Exploration in deserts costs a fortune per drill hole, targeting is often guesswork, and airborne geophysics is expensive. Explorers need cheaper first-pass targeting.
solution: Combine weekly-repeat NISAR L-band radar (open data), Sentinel-1 and, outside North America and Europe, ESA Biomass P-band to map buried paleo-channels, faults and shallow structure in hyper-arid terrain. Deliver target packages per license block, plus a success-fee option.
why_now: NISAR launched in July 2025 with an open-data policy, and ESA's Biomass P-band radar launched in April 2025. Demand for critical minerals is at a peak. Radar penetration only works in very dry ground, so scope is narrow but valuable.
revenue_model: $20-60k per license block. Success fee or royalty on discoveries. Annual subscriptions for geological surveys.
non_obvious_insight: Seeing beneath sand from orbit sounds like science fiction, and it is now possible with free data. The business is expertise and interpretation, not satellites.
first_30_days: Pick two well-studied arid areas as proof cases and reproduce known buried channels. Show results to 20 junior explorers with licenses in arid regions. Sell the first two block packages at a discount for case studies.

title: Humanoid Rentals for Events and Retail
one_liner: The first profitable humanoid job is spectacle: rent Unitree-class robots plus a trained show operator to brands, malls, arenas and trade shows.
customer: Experiential-marketing agencies, retail flagships, stadium and arena marketing teams, trade-show exhibitors, casinos and theme venues. Universities renting lab time come second.
problem: Everyone else pitches humanoids as factory workers, where reliability, safety and ROI are unproven. Brands want a 'robots are here' moment now but cannot buy, program and insure a $16k robot themselves.
solution: Own 6-10 units. Sell packaged experiences (greeter, product demo, dance or boxing, photo-booth persona) with an operator, choreographer, safety marshal and event insurance. Every event doubles as a demo funnel for enterprise pilot inquiries, and later as controlled data capture.
why_now: Unitree's August 2026 IPO (about $9B) and G1 pricing near $16k make fleet capex trivial, so a robot pays back in roughly 10 event-days at $1.5-2.5k a day (my estimate). Humanoid hype is at its peak and marketing budgets are chasing it. China's robot-rental-for-events market is a proof point.
revenue_model: $2-6k a day per robot with operator, $25-60k custom activations, and sponsorship fees. Add an enterprise-pilot lead-gen fee from robot vendors later.
non_obvious_insight: Entertainment tolerates a 70% success rate and teleop, because a stumble is content. The buyer pays for attention, not productivity, so humanoid economics work here years before they work on a factory floor. Note: tariffs or restrictions on Chinese robots are a risk, so keep a non-Chinese unit option.
first_30_days: Buy 2 G1s (about $32k) and build 3 scripted 10-minute acts. Cold-pitch 40 experiential agencies, minor-league teams and mall marketing managers. Book 5 paid weekend events and film content for social proof.

title: Get Paid to Care: Family Caregiver Enrollment
one_liner: A navigator that gets family caregivers onto Medicaid and VA payrolls, then becomes the fiscal intermediary that pays them.
customer: Adult children and spouses (45-70) giving 20+ hours a week of unpaid care to a low-income parent or veteran. Secondary buyers are Area Agencies on Aging, Medicaid managed-care plans and state Medicaid agencies that pay fiscal-intermediary fees.
problem: 59M family caregivers gave 49.5B unpaid hours in 2024 (about $1T) and lose roughly $21k a year in income. Every state has Medicaid self-direction, many pay relatives, and the VA has Veteran-Directed Care. But the rules differ by state, the assessment sets the hours, and agencies and fiscal intermediaries earn more by placing an outside aide.
solution: Phase 1 is a state-by-state 'can I get paid?' screener plus done-with-you enrollment: eligibility, application packet, coaching for the nurse assessment (which sets hours), employee onboarding, timesheet and electronic-visit-verification coaching, and appeals. Phase 2 is to become a licensed fiscal intermediary (payroll, background checks, EVV) in states that allow several vendors, and to bill the state a monthly per-participant fee.
why_now: About $911B in federal Medicaid cuts plus work requirements, 41 states with HCBS waitlists over 600k people (average wait 15 months), and Wisconsin agencies 'not able to take new clients' after the 2026 visa and TPS shocks. States now have to lean on the caregiver already in the house.
revenue_model: Families pay a flat $349-499 per successful enrollment, or a lower fee plus a first-year success fee. Phase 2 adds state or MCO fiscal-intermediary per-member-per-month fees. AAAs can pay for referral-sourced enrollment.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is partly a payment-eligibility problem, not a bodies problem. The gatekeepers who could help families avoid agencies are the agencies and legacy fiscal intermediaries, so no one with a business incentive teaches families the paid-relative pathway.
first_30_days: Pick two states where relatives can be paid and enrollment is open (California's IHSS is the obvious one). Publish the screener and state guides, then capture leads through caregiver support groups, Facebook groups and elder-law firms. Sell a $349 concierge enrollment to the first 20 families and measure approval rate and approved hours.

title: Frozen Models: Long-Term Support for AI Deployments
one_liner: A 'Red Hat for AI models': host specific model versions with a written 5-7 year availability guarantee, reproducibility pack and migration diff-testing, for companies that cannot let their AI change under them.
customer: Model-risk, compliance and QA leads at mid-size banks, insurers, health-tech and pharma-adjacent firms, and legal-tech teams that have validated an AI workflow. Later, AI-companion products and their users, who care about persona continuity.
problem: Frontier labs retire models on 12-18 month cycles. Every retirement forces re-running evals, re-validating prompts and re-documenting for auditors. When OpenAI retired GPT-4o from ChatGPT on Feb 13, 2026, it set off the #Keep4o backlash, proving people and firms treat model behavior as something they depend on.
solution: Pin and host frozen snapshots of open-weight models (and customers' own fine-tunes), with contractual availability through a stated year, a fixed and documented inference stack (versions, quantization, seeds), and a change-control pack (model card, eval suite, audit logs). Add a migration service that replays your real traffic through old and new models and produces a behavior-diff report when you choose to upgrade.
why_now: Deprecation cycles have shortened and the 2026 GPT-4o episode made instability visible outside engineering teams. Regulators and auditors increasingly ask for documented change control on AI systems, and open-weight models are now good enough for many bounded enterprise tasks. Nobody is selling stability itself as the product.
revenue_model: Monthly hosting subscription plus per-token usage, one-time change-control pack fees, and per-migration diff-testing engagements.
non_obvious_insight: Enterprises don't buy the best model, they buy the model that won't change. Each frontier release is a validation event for regulated buyers, so a vendor whose product is boring stability (like Ubuntu LTS or RHEL) has a natural niche, and the cost side is cheap because old open weights run on modest GPUs. The consumer angle (keeping a beloved persona alive) adds emotional stickiness that pure infra players can't match.
first_30_days: Interview 20 model-risk and compliance leads in banks and insurers. Publish a one-page 'frozen model SLA' with pricing. Host three open-weight snapshots on rented GPUs with a documented inference stack. Close two design partners at $2-5k/month and produce the first reproducibility pack.

title: MFP Cash Bridge for Independent Pharmacies
one_liner: Reconciliation plus short-term financing for the cash gap independent pharmacies now carry between dispensing at Medicare's negotiated price and getting the manufacturer refund.
customer: Independent pharmacy owners (about 18,000 US stores) with heavy Medicare Part D volume, who are being asked to float thousands of dollars a week.
problem: The first ten Medicare-negotiated 'maximum fair prices' took effect January 1, 2026. Pharmacies buy at wholesale acquisition cost, dispense at the lower MFP and are refunded later through the Medicare Transaction Facilitator, with refunds due within 14 days but the clock starting only when manufacturers receive the data. An analysis for NCPA estimated weekly cash-flow shortfalls above $10K per pharmacy, and a member survey found over 90% of independents are considering not stocking or have stopped stocking one or more of the drugs.
solution: Step one is software: read pharmacy-management system exports and MTF remittance data, reconcile every MFP claim against refunds received, flag underpayments and late refunds, and forecast next week's cash gap. Step two is an advance product: fund verified pending MFP refunds at a small fee, repaid automatically when the MTF payment lands.
why_now: MFP has been live since January 2026, and cash-flow strain is documented. The second negotiation cycle, effective January 2027, adds 15 more drugs (including semaglutide products), so volume and float will grow sharply. Independent pharmacies are already squeezed by PBM reimbursement and store closures, and wholesalers and PBMs have little incentive to solve this.
revenue_model: $149-299 per pharmacy per month for reconciliation and alerts. 0.5-1.5% fee per advance, with a short 14-30 day duration. Warehouse-line financing spread as volume grows.
non_obvious_insight: This is receivables finance in disguise. Refunds owed by big manufacturers through a federal facilitator are among the best-quality, most verifiable small-business receivables in healthcare. The reconciliation software is the underwriting engine, so a small team can start with software, prove default rates are near zero, and then raise a cheap credit line. Being the trusted data layer also positions you for the 2027 and 2028 waves.
first_30_days: Partner with a state pharmacy association or NCPA-affiliated buying group. Recruit 10-15 pharmacies and ingest exports from PioneerRx, Rx30 or QS/1. Sell a $149/month MFP reconciliation dashboard that finds unpaid refunds. Run a free 'cash gap audit' to generate leads. After 60-90 days of clean data, approach a specialty lender for a small advance pilot.

title: Contingency-Fee 45F Childcare Tax Credit Shop
one_liner: An R&D-credit-style boutique that finds, structures and files the newly expanded employer childcare credit (40%, or 50% for small businesses, capped at $500k/$600k) for firms already spending on childcare.
customer: Mid-market employers (200-5,000 staff) with onsite care or vendor childcare spend: hospitals, manufacturers, universities, credit unions and restaurant chains. Referral channel: their CPA firms.
problem: The 45F credit was rarely used under its old cap. From January 1, 2026 the credit rose to 40% (50% small business) with $500k ($600k) caps. Eligibility turns on contract structure, licensing, enrollment open to employees and documentation, and it interacts with the new $7,500 DCFSA limit. Generalist CPAs don't know it and CFOs have never claimed it.
solution: A two-week diagnostic reviews contracts and spend, restructures where needed (for example, reserved-slot agreements with licensed local centers or consortium models), computes the credit and files the forms alongside the client's CPA. Reserved-slot deals also give centers guaranteed enrollment, which helps supply.
why_now: The changes took effect January 2026, employers set 2027 benefit budgets in Q4 2026, and the first full filing season under the new rules is early 2027.
revenue_model: Contingency fee of 15-20% of credit claimed (a $250k credit yields $40-50k). Add-on brokerage fee for slot-reservation contracts.
non_obvious_insight: A $500k cap means the credit can fund a whole classroom's worth of care per employer. The constraint is know-how, not money, and reserved-slot contracts turn a tax credit into childcare supply, a desert fix hidden in the tax code.
first_30_days: Partner with a tax attorney or CPA who has done R&D or WOTC credits. Build a list of 200 employers advertising childcare benefits (job posts, hospital filings). Publish a two-page 45F guide and a free eligibility screen. Aim for 3 signed contingency engagements.

title: Settlement Passports for Florida High-Rise Condos
one_liner: A satellite-radar settlement history for every Florida condo tower, sold as the cheap first page of the milestone-inspection and reserve-study file.
customer: Florida condo associations and the licensed engineers and property managers who run their milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies; secondary buyers are master-policy underwriters, lenders and buyers' agents doing condo diligence.
problem: Carriers want structural documents before they bind a master policy, SIRS and milestone inspections are mandatory for 3+ story buildings, and special assessments run $50K-$200K+ per unit. Boards cannot tell whether their building is stable or sinking until an engineer bills for scoping. A 2024 University of Miami InSAR study found 35 Miami Beach to Sunny Isles buildings subsiding 2-8 cm over 2016-2023, and no commercial product packages this for boards.
solution: Process free Sentinel-1 radar (2015 onward), ESA archive radar for the 1990s-2010s, and newly public NISAR L-band data into a per-building vertical-motion trend. Add differential tilt across the footprint and a comparison against neighbours built on similar fill. Deliver a 3-page Settlement Passport plus a monitoring feed, positioned as a screening indicator that sharpens inspection scope, with an engineer partner signing off. It is not a substitute for the inspection.
why_now: Florida's post-Surfside SB 4-D inspection and reserve-study mandates are now enforced and carriers demand documents. NISAR L-band data has been free through ASF since the July 20, 2026 public release, adding to the Sentinel-1 record. Peer-reviewed proof that InSAR resolves individual Miami towers exists but has not been productized. Reinsurance is softening while condo retail insurance is still squeezed.
revenue_model: $900-$2,500 per building for the initial passport and $300/yr for monitoring. Wholesale price of about $400 to engineering firms who bundle it into SIRS work. $100/building/yr portfolio contracts for management companies.
non_obvious_insight: InSAR is treated as an academic or pipeline-monitoring tool, but the buyer with a legal deadline and a real budget is a condo board that must assemble a structural file. Persistent-scatterer InSAR works best on concrete high-rises, the exact asset at issue. The 10-30 year archive can also show a building has been stable for decades, which makes it a positive underwriting asset for the many buildings that are fine, not just a warning label.
first_30_days: Run the free Sentinel-1 stack for about 400 buildings on the Miami-Dade and Broward barrier islands. Offer one free passport to each of 15 engineering firms and 5 management companies, and sign 2 engineers as resellers. Then charge the first 10 boards facing reserve-study or insurance-renewal deadlines.

title: Certified Scrap Kill for Aircraft Parts
one_liner: A mobile crew and app that destroys, photographs and certifies scrapped aircraft parts so they can never resurface as fake 'serviceable' parts, and sells the segregated metal.
customer: Regional airline stores and quality departments, Part 145 repair stations, lessors managing teardowns and part-outs, and engine and component shops. They pay a per-event fee, partly offset by a share of the alloy value.
problem: Every airline is supposed to mutilate parts that are beyond economical repair or time-expired so they cannot re-enter the supply chain. On the floor, the scrap cage gets emptied by a metals dealer on a handshake. Serial plates are sometimes cut off and sometimes not. Techs and stores people know that 'scrapped' units can turn up months later 'overhauled' at a broker with a tidy set of documents. The airline also carries the paper trail risk. If a fake part traces back to your serial number, you are in the investigation. Meanwhile titanium and nickel-alloy scrap is sold mixed at a low commodity price, because nobody segregates it.
solution: A van with a shear or plasma cutter, a tag punch and a phone app. Per drum or per pallet, the crew scans and photographs part number and serial number before destruction, destroys the part in a way that defeats reuse, photographs it again after, and pushes a hash-stamped certificate of destruction into the customer's inventory system. This removes the item from their books and gives quality staff and lessor auditors an unbroken chain of custody. Scrap is segregated by alloy and sold to specialty metal buyers, which funds the service.
why_now: Scrutiny of unapproved and counterfeit parts has stayed high since the 2023 forged-release-certificate scandal involving CFM56 parts. The FAA has long-standing guidance on detecting and reporting suspected unapproved parts (AC 21-29), and lessors and insurers keep tightening audit requirements. Fleet retirements of older regional aircraft in 2025-2026 are creating unusually large scrap volumes. Cheap phone-based photo and OCR capture removes the need for special hardware.
revenue_model: Fee per destruction event or per kilogram ($X per event plus a metal revenue share, typically netting near zero out of pocket for the airline). Annual chain-of-custody programs for lessors and MROs. Later, sell certified segregated alloy lots to aerospace melters at a premium.
non_obvious_insight: Airlines treat scrap as a solved cost center. Techs know it is the weakest link in traceability. The buyer's pain is not the cost of scrap, it is being named in the paper trail of a counterfeit. Whoever owns certified destruction owns a record that every auditor, lessor and regulator increasingly wants. The metal value pays for the service, so the airline's out-of-pocket is close to zero, and that removes the budget objection.
first_30_days: Choose one metro with a regional hub plus several 145 shops. Buy a used band saw or plasma cutter and a tag punch, and line up a metals dealer that will accept segregated alloys. Have an aviation attorney draft a certificate of destruction that cites the operator's own manual procedure and AC 21-29. Offer the first scrap-cage clear-out free to 3-5 quality managers, with before and after photos and a metal check. Ask two lessor technical reps for introductions, since they carry the bigger volume.

title: Credit Union Tokenized Deposit Network
one_liner: Give thousands of small credit unions a shared 24/7 tokenized-deposit settlement network so they can answer the 'war for deposits' together instead of losing it one by one.
customer: Credit unions ($500M-$10B assets), state leagues and CUSOs, and later their members and local merchants.
problem: Banks describe the stablecoin fight as a '$6 trillion war for deposits' (CoinDesk, 2026-09-14). No single credit union has the scale to run its own token or build 24/7 settlement, and Zelle-style networks are controlled by big banks. Members get weekday-hours payments between institutions.
solution: A CUSO-owned network of tokenized member deposits (not a stablecoin at first), starting with 24/7 credit-union-to-credit-union settlement for shared branching and member P2P, then bill pay and merchant acceptance. A licensed trust-bank or custody partner handles the token layer and reserves.
why_now: The OCC charter wave (Circle 2026-07-10, Coinbase April, Bridge and Crypto.com conditional) has made compliant token infrastructure available to partner with. Citi and Coinbase launched corporate stablecoin acceptance on 2026-09-28, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
revenue_model: Network transaction fees, SaaS to member credit unions, and a share of reserve income on the settlement layer.
non_obvious_insight: The cooperative structure is the unfair advantage. Credit unions already share ATMs, branching and core processing through CUSOs, so a shared money layer is a natural extension that gives 4,500 small institutions scale none could build alone.
first_30_days: Get LOIs from five credit unions through one state league. Run a paper pilot for inter-credit-union treasury settlement with a partner trust bank, and charge pilot fees for design work and integration.

title: Exit Ramps for Dying AI Platforms
one_liner: A converter plus fixed-price migration service that turns Flowise flows, OpenAI Agent Builder graphs and Assistants API integrations into portable, regression-tested code.
customer: AI automation agencies that have 5-50 client agents built on Flowise, Agent Builder or the Assistants API, and in-house AI teams at SMEs that have no engineer to spare. They pay per migrated agent.
problem: Three AI platforms are being killed within about 90 days. The Assistants API shut down on 26 Aug 2026. Agent Builder shuts down on 30 Nov 2026. Flowise was archived in mid-Aug 2026 and its core team leaves on 31 Aug. Non-technical teams built visual flows they cannot maintain as raw code. A Flowise insider says forkers 'own dependency updates, security patches, and model API churn indefinitely, and the contributor community that used to absorb that work is dispersing.' A commenter says telling non-engineers to maintain a TypeScript codebase 'is not a real answer.'
solution: Build importers for Flowise chatflow JSON, Agent Builder workflow exports and Assistants objects (assistants, threads, vector stores, files). They feed a neutral intermediate representation. Exporters then emit (a) Agents SDK / Responses API code, (b) n8n workflows, (c) Langflow. The differentiator is a parity proof. Historical conversation logs are replayed against old and new stacks, and the agency receives a behavioral-diff report it can send to its client. The output is plain, readable code that a coding agent such as Claude Code can maintain. Flowise itself says developers are moving to coding agents because 'rigid workflow low code approach quickly hits the limit.'
why_now: The Assistants API shutdown (26 Aug 2026), the Agent Builder deadline (30 Nov 2026) and the Flowise archive (Aug 2026) all land in one quarter, which forces spending on a real deadline. Coding agents now make code-first output maintainable by non-experts. Flowise has 55.5k stars and 25k forks, so the stranded installed base is large.
revenue_model: Fixed-price migration of $500-2,500 per agent. An agency plan of $199/mo keeps flows mirrored in the intermediate representation with a nightly 'can I still leave?' test. The free converter CLI is the lead magnet.
non_obvious_insight: The demand is a deadline plus a maintenance gap, not a tooling gap. Evidence: OpenAI's deprecations page gives the Agent Builder shutdown as 30 Nov 2026 and the Assistants API as 26 Aug 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations). Flowise's sunset notice sets the code freeze, the archive and the end of core-team support (https://flowiseai.com/sunset). The GitHub repo shows 55.5k stars, 25k forks and 699 open issues (https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise). The HN thread quotes the 'not a real answer' complaint and notes that OpenAI's own Agent Builder is also going away (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49176920). Agencies that resell agents to clients are the buyers, and they carry portfolio risk that a single hobbyist does not. The parity report is what they sell on to their clients.
first_30_days: Week 1: mine the Flowise Discord, GitHub issues and r/n8n for stranded users. Ship a free 'flowise-to-n8n / Agents SDK' CLI that handles the 3 most common node types. Weeks 2-3: cold-DM 40 agencies and sell 5-10 pilot migrations at $750, prioritizing Agent Builder users before the 30 Nov deadline. Week 4: turn the manual steps in those migrations into automated exporters and publish before/after parity reports as case studies.

title: Vet-Side Passport Network for Pets and Horses
one_liner: Give official veterinarians a certificate copilot that turns microchip-anchored records into error-free health certificates and a verifiable travel dossier that carriers and shippers can check before departure.
customer: Official Veterinarian practices in the UK and EU (and accredited vets in the US), plus pet and horse transport companies. Ferry, tunnel and airline operators are later payers for pre-verified manifests.
problem: Since 22 April 2026 UK-based owners must use single-entry Animal Health Certificates, 11-14 pages issued by an Official Veterinarian, instead of EU-issued passports. Vet time per certificate is heavy, the timing windows for vaccination and treatment are easy to get wrong, and a chip-number or wording error means refusal at the border. Horse shippers juggle TRACES, FEI and national passport systems separately.
solution: Software for vet practices that pulls microchip and vaccination data from practice-management systems, imports lab results, applies a country-rule engine with timing windows, pre-fills the certificate and flags errors before the vet signs. It issues the owner a portable dossier with a verifiable signature and QR code. A pre-flight checker lets shippers validate multi-animal consignments before departure.
why_now: The April 2026 EU rule change, wider TRACES digital processing, and constant UK-EU rule churn mean a maintained rules engine has recurring value. Owners are newly forced into per-trip certificates.
revenue_model: $100-190 per OV per month plus $10-20 per certificate, shipper plans from about $300 a month, and later per-manifest fees from carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The animal identity problem is already solved: microchips and horse life numbers are global standards. What is missing is trust and issuance friction, and a licensed vet is the human trust anchor. You do not need new identity infrastructure. You sell the trust anchor a better pen, and animals avoid the privacy fights that slow human wallets.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 OV practices near Dover and Folkestone, where certificate volume is highest, and 3 horse shippers. Start with the UK-to-EU Animal Health Certificate only, filling PDFs semi-manually. Charge per certificate, measure vet minutes saved and rejection rate, and publish the numbers to win the next 50 practices.

title: Hardening Passport: Proof That Earns Premium Credits
one_liner: A contractor-paid evidence layer that turns every roof, vent and 5-ft-zone job into an insurer-acceptable credit claim or parcel-score appeal.
customer: Roofing, vent-retrofit and defensible-space contractors (5-50 crews) in Colorado and California, paying per verified job. Homeowners get the packet bundled with the work.
problem: Insiders assume mitigation credits fail because insurers do not want to give them. Colorado HB25-1182 (in force July 1 2026) now forces disclosure of the parcel score, credit for documented mitigation and an appeal. But homeowners cannot produce insurer-grade proof. One owner reports 'a thousand bucks' off after a $75,000 metal roof, and Boulder's rebate is capped at $500. Contractors lose sales because the payback cannot be shown.
solution: A phone capture flow for crews: geotagged before/after photos, roof class and vent model certificates, 5-ft clearance measurements, all mapped to IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home criteria and each carrier's credit form. It outputs a ready-to-file credit packet and, in Colorado, an appeal letter citing the disclosed score. Contractors use it as a sales line ('we file your discount').
why_now: HB25-1182 took effect July 1 2026 and California AB 75 became operative the same day. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington. This is the first time a statute gives proof a place to land.
revenue_model: $49-99 per verified job or $199/month per crew. Later, carriers pay per accepted credit, and verified-hardening portfolio data is sold to carriers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: Scoring is commoditizing (MSCI paid only $120M cash for First Street), but neutral proof is still scarce. Insurers cannot advocate for the policyholder, so the party with the incentive and the field access is the contractor.
first_30_days: Sign 5 Front Range roofers or mitigation crews. Build the capture flow as a web app around the IBHS checklist. Hand-assemble 50 packets, file them with 3 carriers, and track the acceptance rate as the core proof metric.

title: Verified-Real Dating Portraits Shot by Wedding Photographers
one_liner: A consumer brand that rents wedding photographers' dead winter months to shoot candid-directed dating and profile portraits, delivered with a signed 'real photo' certificate.
customer: Single adults aged 25-45 in the top 20 US metros paying $179-299 per session. Secondary channel: matchmakers and dating coaches buying sessions for their clients.
problem: Wedding photographers earn most of their income in a compressed May-October window and sit mostly idle from November to March, with skills and gear already paid for. Meanwhile dating profiles are flooded with AI-generated and heavily retouched photos, so users and matches increasingly distrust every photo. Existing options are cheap AI headshot apps (the very thing everyone distrusts), generic corporate headshot studios that make stiff LinkedIn photos, and a few dating-photo studios with model-y aesthetics. Nobody is selling authenticity as a verifiable, human-shot product.
solution: A productized 60-minute walk-and-talk shoot across three locations using wedding-style directing prompts ('walk toward me and tell me the worst first date you've had') that get natural laughter from stiff people in about 90 seconds. Delivery is 15 edited photos in 48 hours following a dating shot list (full-body, hobby, social proof, pet, non-selfie smile). Each set ships with a 'Real Photo Certificate': Content Credentials (C2PA) from supported cameras, a no-generative-AI editing policy, and a public verification page users can link in their bio. Supply comes from wedding photographers trained in a 90-minute module. The platform handles booking, payment, brand, marketing and QC and keeps 30-35%.
why_now: AI-generated profile photos are now common enough that dating apps have leaned on photo and face verification. Several major camera makers now ship Content Credentials support in newer bodies or firmware, so provenance is technically feasible for small studios. Wedding photographers are also under margin pressure as couples trim coverage hours and guest counts, so winter income is increasingly attractive. 2026 is the first year 'proof a human made this' has real consumer value.
revenue_model: $199-299 per session with a 30-35% platform take. Upsells include a $39 'profile audit' and a re-shoot at 6 months. B2B2C packages for matchmakers and dating coaches at $150 per client.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce skill isn't lighting, it's getting a stiff stranger to laugh convincingly on cue, which wedding photographers do 40 times a summer. The photographer's marginal cost in January is close to zero, so supply arrives almost free while every competitor pays full-time studio rents.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and recruit 6 wedding photographers who complain publicly about winter. Run 20 pilot shoots at a $99 launch price, sourced from local Instagram/Reddit dating communities, run clubs and singles events, and from 5 matchmakers and dating coaches. Ask each client for before/after match counts (self-reported) and permission to publish testimonials. Register a public verification page for each set. Charge full price from shoot 21 onward.

title: Auto-to-Defense Conversion Accelerator for Tier-2 Suppliers
one_liner: A fixed-price certification package plus matched RFQs that turn idle auto-parts plants into qualified defense and aerospace suppliers.
customer: Tier-2 and tier-3 automotive stampers, machiners and casting shops with 25-250 employees in the Midwest and South. Defense primes co-fund supplier development.
problem: OEM robot orders are down 25% and autos lost 4.5k jobs in August, while defense money is flowing (Hadrian raised $1.37B; it holds an $80M Army deal). Auto suppliers have capacity and process discipline (IATF), but defense work needs AS9100, ITAR registration, DFARS specialty-metals tracking and NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 (phase 2 is scheduled for November 2026). Consultants sell these piecemeal.
solution: A 90-day package: gap assessment, IATF-to-AS9100 crosswalk, ITAR registration, an NIST 800-171 plan on a managed enclave, DFARS specialty-metals tracking, and a mock audit, delivered mostly by templates and a small compliance team. It ends with RFQs matched from primes looking for capacity.
why_now: The auto retreat leaves capacity idle, defense capital is at record levels, and CMMC requirements are phasing in. Primes need more sub-tier suppliers.
revenue_model: $35-80k fixed fee per shop or $3-5k a month for the managed enclave. Success fee on first contract. RFQ-routing fees from primes.
non_obvious_insight: Auto suppliers already have the hard part (process discipline, volume) but are invisible to primes for lack of paperwork. Selling capacity conversion instead of compliance opens the prime's supplier-development budget. The CMMC consultant market is crowded, so the wedge is the RFQ match, not the audit.
first_30_days: Recruit five shops through chambers of commerce, auto-supplier associations and state MEP centers. Partner with a C3PAO and a GCC High MSP. Meet two primes' supplier-development teams about co-funding. Land two paid pilots at about $25k.

title: Tell Us Once: US Death-Event Switchboard
one_liner: Verify an executor once, then let agents notify and close dozens of institutions for you, building toward a reusable 'authority to act' credential the institutions accept.
customer: Executors and surviving families pay, with distribution through funeral homes, estate attorneys and employers or insurers. Institutions later pay per verified case.
problem: US executors call dozens of banks, card issuers, utilities and subscription companies, each demanding its own certified death certificate, letters and forms. The deceased's identity is exposed to fraud. The UK has 'Tell Us Once', the US has nothing, and the brief finds no dominant software owner of the estate close-out workflow.
solution: The executor uploads the death certificate, ID and letters. The system verifies them once, then voice and browser agents run institution-specific playbooks: credit bureau alerts, identity locks, marketing suppression, subscription and utility cancellations or transfers, date-of-death balance requests and claim forms. A status board tracks every account, and human ops handle exceptions. Over time it issues a verified executor credential institutions accept by API.
why_now: Voice agents that navigate phone trees and hold queues, and browser agents that complete web forms, reached usable reliability in 2025-26. Digital ID wallets are spreading. Insurer and employer channels such as Empathy (50M+ covered policyholders) show buyers for bereavement services, but Empathy is not a close-out execution layer.
revenue_model: $199-$399 flat per estate ($99 wholesale to funeral homes), $10-$40 per verified case from institutions, and insurer or employer benefit contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is repeated verification, not the work itself. A reusable, verified authority credential collapses 60 identical fights into one and gives institutions a fraud-reduction reason to cooperate.
first_30_days: Build playbooks for the top 30 institutions (big banks, card issuers, brokers, telecoms, streaming, credit bureaus). Sell 25 human-in-the-loop cases through 5 funeral homes at $149. Record each institution's requirements to build the data moat.

title: Reusable Trust Passport for Bio-AI Access
angle: Pairing 1: AI agents & agent economy x Biotech tools / synbio / lab automation
one_liner: One neutral, portable verification that a biotech or academic lab is legitimate, bound to that lab's agent keys, so frontier AI vendors and DNA/reagent suppliers can accept its agent-placed orders without repeating the diligence.
customer: Small and mid-size biotechs, academic labs and CROs that need relaxed AI safeguards and want agents to order DNA, oligos and reagents. Secondary payers are AI vendors and suppliers who pay per verified check.
problem: On September 17, 2026 Anthropic launched its Life Sciences Verification Program (credential, security and ethics-oversight review, 30-day data retention) and expected hundreds of organizations in week one. Other AI providers, DNA synthesis vendors and cloud labs will each build their own version. Small labs lack SOC 2-style security paperwork, organized IBC documentation or an ethics-oversight file, so they queue or get denied. Machine identities already outnumber humans about 109 to 1 and there is no shared 'know your agent' standard for bio orders.
solution: A one-time dossier (organization identity, IBC/IACUC registration, named biosafety officer, lightweight security review, data-handling policy) issued as a verifiable credential tied to the lab's agent keys. AI vendors and suppliers accept it for access tiers and agent-placed orders, and the credential is continuously monitored and revoked if an IBC approval lapses. Include a readiness checklist and concierge help to complete the paperwork.
why_now: Verification programs started in September 2026, creating an immediate backlog and duplicative-paperwork problem. Agent-order volume is growing, and synthesis-screening rules and frontier-lab safeguards are tightening at the same time.
revenue_model: Flat verification fee ($1.5-5K one-time plus annual renewal), per-check fees from vendors and AI providers, and an enterprise tier for CRO networks and shared core facilities.
non_obvious_insight: Frontier labs cannot be each other's trust anchor, which is why an accredited third-party reviewer that several of them accept is valuable. This is the Vanta/Plaid pattern applied to bio access, and the first concierge revenue comes from the backlog, before any network effect exists.
first_30_days: Build the 'verification readiness' checklist and offer a $2.5K flat concierge service to the first 20 labs that applied. Talk to 3 mid-tier DNA/oligo vendors and 2 cloud labs about accepting your dossier for agent orders. Publish an open template so vendors see you as the standards-setter, then charge for review and monitoring.

title: Tamper-Proof Photo Evidence for Produce Rejections
angle: Pairing 2: Food & agriculture x Cybersecurity/deepfake fraud/identity verification/scams
one_liner: A capture-only app that produces AI-proof receiving-dock photo and video evidence so shippers can contest bogus load rejections and reroute rejected produce to salvage buyers within hours.
customer: Mid-size grower-shippers and brokers of berries, leafy greens, tomatoes and other perishables (Salinas, Yuma, Nogales and Florida corridors). PACA-licensed receivers who want to prove genuine rejections are a second segment, and produce factoring companies a third.
problem: Produce is sold before it arrives, and when market prices fall, a rejection on 'condition' photos is a well-known way to force a price cut. Shippers have photos, phone calls and slow inspections. Generative editing makes photos cheap to fabricate or alter, and neither side can prove authenticity (IC3 notes many victims cannot tell AI was involved). Rejected loads then rot or are dumped because salvage rerouting is slow, adding to food waste.
solution: In-app capture only, with device attestation, GPS, server timestamp, pallet-tag and lot-code OCR, Bluetooth temperature-logger tie-in, a standard shot list built from USDA quality standards, and a signed content-credential manifest. Each load gets a shareable verification link that both parties, a USDA or third-party inspector and PACA arbitrators can open, plus a live tele-inspection mode. Once a rejection is verified, an eight-hour clock starts and alerts go to salvage buyers, processors and food banks.
why_now: By 2026 photo editing with generative tools is trivial and undetectable to most people. The farm labor shortage means late harvests and more variable quality. The EU is moving toward binding food-waste cuts (30% in retail by 2030), which makes measured diversion valuable. Content credentials and device attestation are now standard on phones.
revenue_model: $4-8 per load or $400-1,500 a month per shipper, a 5-8% fee on the recovered value of rerouted salvage, and a co-sell with produce factors who freeze advances during disputes.
non_obvious_insight: In produce, a bad photo is a price-negotiation weapon, and whoever controls the trusted photo controls the money. The wedge is the shipper and the factor, who lose most from doubtful rejections, not the receiver. Verified evidence also turns each rejection from a bargaining event into clean market data.
first_30_days: Offer a free 30-day pilot to 3 grower-shippers in one corridor and capture their next 100 loads. Measure dispute-resolution time before and after. Recruit a produce factoring company or PACA attorney as a co-seller. Build the shot list from USDA grade standards.
